web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What Henry Hub strip, FCF durability, and Range Resources merger dilution are already priced into EQT at $52.81?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. In commodities, the market always prices the next trough before the last one is forgotten.
epigraph.author: Howard Marks, The Most Important Thing (paraphrased)

web_blocks.html: At the November 13, 2026 close of $52.81, EQT holds a $33.04B market cap [23, 24]. Its enterprise value is $42.06B after $5.5B of net debt and PipeBox non-controlling interests [23, 24]. On trailing results, EQT trades at 12.52x P/E, 6.41x EV/EBITDA, 8.67x P/FCF, and 1.30x Price-to-Book [23, 24]. Its dividend yield is 1.26%, or $0.67 per share [23, 24]. Forward P/E rises to 15.51x as estimates reflect softer gas prices and new shares for the Range Resources (RRC) merger [24, 26].

EQT trades at $52.81, down 22.61% from its $68.24 high [23]. To see what is priced in, we run a Reverse DCF rather than guessing a target price. We apply an 8.5% WACC and a 2.0% terminal growth rate. At $42.06B EV, the market implies ~$2.73B in steady-state unlevered FCF, or ~$2.45B–$2.60B in annual levered FCF. Compare that with EQT's $2,802M FY2025 FCF and $283M Q3 2026 FCF (~$1.13B annualized during 21 Bcfe of shut-ins) [1, 28]. At $52.81, the market prices in $2.85–$3.05/MMBtu Henry Hub gas. That matches the EIA's November 2026 forecast of $2.87/MMBtu for Winter 2026–2027 and $2.88/MMBtu for 2027 [25].

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF & Henry Hub Sensitivity: Implied Equity Value Across Mid-Cycle Gas Regimes (Standalone vs. Pro Forma RRC)
web_blocks.takeaway: At $52.81, EQT prices in ~$2.90/MMBtu mid-cycle Henry Hub with zero credit for $325M-$600M Range synergies [23, 25, 26]. Pro forma target prices ($40 / $64 / $76) reflect ~856.6M combined shares (625.6M EQT + ~231M RRC) less ~$9.02B net debt and PipeBox NCI.

web_blocks.html: The second weight on EQT's multiple is the October 26, 2026 all-stock Range Resources merger [26]. Under the 0.987x exchange ratio, Range holders will own ~27% of the $50B+ EV combined firm [26]. EQT will issue about 231M new shares when the deal closes in Q1 2027 [26]. Merger arbitrage funds short EQT and buy Range ($51.83 vs. $52.12 implied, a 0.6% spread) [23, 26]. That creates short-term selling pressure on EQT while investors wait for antitrust clearance and synergy proof [26]. Wall Street targets cluster near $66–$68/share, yet buyers will not pay up before closing [27].

web_blocks.caption: Live Valuation & Quality Matrix: EQT vs. Appalachian Upstream & Midstream Peers (Session 2026-11-13)
web_blocks.takeaway: EQT trades at 6.41x EV/EBITDA and 8.67x P/FCF—a slight discount to Antero (7.30x EV/EBITDA) and a sharp discount to pure-play midstream tollbooths KMI (13.29x) and WMB (17.39x), despite owning Equitrans and MVP [23, 24].

web_blocks.html: Peer multiples show why EQT sits in a valuation middle ground [23, 24]. Pure-play pipeline operators Kinder Morgan (13.29x EV/EBITDA) and Williams (17.39x EV/EBITDA) trade at more than double EQT's 6.41x multiple [23, 24]. Upstream peer Expand Energy trades lower at 4.48x EV/EBITDA because it lacks owned gathering pipes [23, 24]. Antero Resources trades at 7.30x EV/EBITDA on stronger NGL liquids pricing [23, 24]. EQT owns $1.21B of midstream operating income, yet still wears a driller's multiple [1, 23].

web_blocks.mechanism: Like EQT integrating Equitrans and Range Resources, CNQ bought distressed/stranded long-life reserves and midstream egress during commodity troughs (2017 Shell/Marathon oil sands deal) while trading at 6x–7x EV/EBITDA, then de-levered rapidly and re-rated once free cash flow inflected.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: CNQ cut net debt from >$22B CAD in 2017 to <$10B CAD by 2023, expanded FCF per share by >3x, and delivered >180% total return over 2017–2023 as the market stopped valuing it as a high-beta driller.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Low-decline, vertically integrated resource majors only re-rate from 6x EV/EBITDA toward 8x+ after merger-arbitrage overhang clears and net debt hits management's structural floor.

web_blocks.html: EQT's own ten-year history confirms the same point: the stock is neither bubbly nor distressed. At 8.67x P/FCF and 6.41x EV/EBITDA, EQT sits in the lower half of its post-2020 range [23, 24]. That discount reflects EIA's $2.88/MMBtu 2027 gas forecast and pre-close merger arbitrage [25, 26]. A move toward 7.5x–8.0x EV/EBITDA requires post-close synergies above $325M/year and Henry Hub above $3.25/MMBtu on LNG demand [25, 26].

Decision Triggers: Initiate a starter buy on a pullback to $48.00–$50.50 support (2.25:1 R:R to $64.00 Base) or a Stage 2 volume reclaim above $55.50+ (≥1.3x 30D volume); stand aside on a breakdown below the $44.50 invalidation stop.

book_paragraphs: Walk up to any energy trading desk in Houston or New York and ask why EQT sits at $52.81 when it owns the lowest-cost gas molecule in North America, and you will hear two words before you finish your coffee: strip and arb.

Let us unpack both of those words together, because if you do not understand what the market is already discounting into $52.81, you will mistake a cyclical reset for a broken business—or worse, mistake a cheap multiple for a free lunch.

First, look at what $52.81 actually implies in a Reverse DCF. With 625.55 million shares out and $5.5 billion in net debt (plus non-controlling PipeBox JV interests), EQT's enterprise value is $42.06 billion. If we demand an 8.5% annual return—fair for an investment-grade energy producer with commodity beta—and assume 2.0% long-term inflation growth, the business only needs to generate about $2.7 billion of steady-state free cash flow a year to justify today's price.

Now check the scoreboard we built in Chapter 6. In FY2025, EQT generated $2,802 million of free cash flow. Even in a choppy 2026 where management intentionally curtailed 21 Bcfe in Q3 to avoid dumping gas into a weak autumn tape, EQT's trailing P/FCF sits at 8.67x—an 11.5% free cash flow yield on equity. So why isn't the stock at $68?

Because the EIA just cut its Winter 2026–2027 Henry Hub forecast by 16% to $2.87 per MMBtu, and its full-year 2027 forecast to $2.88 per MMBtu, citing mild early-November weather and swelling storage. At $2.88 Henry Hub, EQT does not break—its unlevered breakeven is ~$2.00—but its windfall cash flow compresses. The market at $52.81 is pricing EQT cleanly for ~$2.90 gas, giving you zero free credit for a cold winter, zero credit for LNG export pull, and zero credit for the $325 million to $600 million in synergies from the Range Resources merger.

And that brings us to the second word: arb. When EQT announced its $13 billion-plus all-stock acquisition of Range Resources on October 26, 2026—offering 0.987 EQT shares for every Range share—merger arbitrage funds immediately did what they always do. They bought Range at a discount and shorted EQT to lock in the spread. Notice that Range closed Friday at $51.83 while 0.987 times EQT's $52.81 is $52.12. That razor-thin 0.6% spread tells you two things: Wall Street expects the deal to close in Q1 2027, and EQT's stock has been wearing a temporary arbitrageur's anchor.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When you see a premier operator trading at 6.4x EV/EBITDA and 8.7x trailing FCF while its midstream peers trade at 13x to 17x, ask yourself what must go right for that gap to close. For EQT, it doesn't require $5.00 gas—it just requires closing Range cleanly, banking the $325M+ synergies, and letting winter and 2027 LNG liquefaction terminals clear the storage overhang.

book_subsections.title: Peer Benchmarking: Upstream Scale vs. Midstream Multiples
paragraphs: Look across the peer table from Friday's close. Expand Energy (EXE) trades cheaper on headline multiples—4.48x EV/EBITDA and 7.67x P/E—because it lacks EQT's owned gathering and Mountain Valley Pipeline tollbooth. Antero Resources (AR) trades at 7.30x EV/EBITDA and 6.74x P/FCF, enjoying strong NGL liquids pricing and a healthier chart above its 200-day moving average ($37.02 vs. $38.74 close).

Meanwhile, pure-play pipeline giants Kinder Morgan (KMI) at 13.29x EV/EBITDA and Williams (WMB) at 17.39x EV/EBITDA trade at more than double EQT's multiple. Why? Because Wall Street pays up for fee-based predictability and penalizes commodity variance. EQT sits in the middle: it owns $1.21 billion of annual midstream operating income, yet the market still prices the entire enterprise at an upstream driller's 6.4x multiple. That valuation tension is the core of our Base Case upside to $64.00—and our Bear Case risk to $40.00 if gas lingers near $2.35.

book_subsections.title: The Range Resources Merger Math: Dilution Today, Scale Tomorrow
paragraphs: Let us walk through the Range Resources math on the back of an envelope, because you should never take a management synergy slide at face value without checking the share count first. Range brings roughly 2.50 Bcfe/d of liquids-rich Appalachian production and $138 million in Q3 2026 free cash flow, plus deep NGL processing infrastructure that complements EQT's dry-gas core. In exchange, EQT is issuing 0.987 shares per Range share, handing Range shareholders roughly 27% of the combined company.

In the short run, issuing ~231 million new shares dilutes near-term EPS—which is why Forward P/E steps up from 12.52x trailing to 15.51x forward. Over a 24-month window, however, management targets $325 million in base annual synergies and a long-term pathway above $600 million, while pushing the combined unlevered FCF breakeven below $2.00 per MMBtu across 30+ years of inventory. Remember our Canadian Natural Resources parallel: CNQ endured years of skepticism and share digestion after its 2017 megadeal before the market rewarded its low-decline free cash flow machine with a higher multiple. EQT is walking that exact same road, which is why timing your entry matters as much as picking the asset.

book_subsections.title: What the Reverse DCF Tells Us About Margin of Safety
paragraphs: Think of Reverse DCF as translating a stock price into a plain-English bet. At $52.81, the market is not demanding heroic $4.50 natural gas or flawless M&A execution—it is merely asking for ~$2.90 per MMBtu mid-cycle Henry Hub and ~$2.7 billion of steady-state annual free cash flow. That is a reasonable, grounded expectation that matches the EIA's November 2026 forecast.

Why, then, do we refuse to pay $52.81 right now? Because in cyclical commodities, 'fairly priced' is not enough—you want a margin of safety against mild-winter drawdowns and merger-integration hiccups. Buying at $48.00–$50.50 shifts the odds decisively onto your side of the table.

book_subsections.title: Why EV/EBITDA Matters More Than P/E for Natural Gas Majors
paragraphs: Whenever you compare EQT against peers like Antero Resources, Range Resources, or Expand Energy, never rely on trailing P/E alone. Commodity producers experience sharp swings in non-cash depreciation, depletion, and amortization (DD&A) as well as unrealized mark-to-market gains or losses on their hedge books. Those accounting items can make a cash-rich quarter look artificially depressed or make a hedged quarter look artificially boomed.

Instead, anchor your valuation work on Enterprise Value to EBITDA and unlevered Free Cash Flow yield—both of which strip out hedge-accounting noise and capital-structure differences. At 6.41x EV/EBITDA and 8.67x trailing P/FCF, EQT is priced modestly below its long-term asset quality, waiting only for the Range Resources merger close and clearer 2027 gas balances to unlock a re-rating.
